Working notes:
- Task: route large east-region requests (shipment, claim, invoice, refund) to the correct desk.
- Options seen: A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office (sometimes truncated).
- Evidence: REQ-2400 shipment from Field Sales was accepted with option C (+1.00). Every later C attempt (REQ-2401–2409) was rejected: “option C is not valid.” Rejections span shipment, claim, invoice, refund, multiple sender desks, and urgency/no-rush wording.
- Conclusion: C is not a general valid routing choice. Do not pick C merely because the request is east-region or mentions the regional office. The single C success is insufficient/anomalous.
- Use A or B only. No observed outcomes for A/B yet, so avoid overfitting. Possible heuristic: B for explicit urgency (“client asking twice,” “before end of day”); A for “no rush.” Verify with feedback.
- Sender name/desk did not determine validity; “second attempt” did not help.
- If option C appears with different wording, re-evaluate rather than assuming invalid.

Option C: one old acceptance (REQ-2400 shipment, Field Sales), but all later C attempts rejected across types/senders/wording. Treat C as invalid except for an exact repeat of a known success combo.

Option A: not generally valid and not simply “no rush.” New evidence:
- Accepted: REQ-2412 invoice, Regional Ops, “No rush…confirm”; REQ-2413 refund, Regional Ops, “through regional office”; REQ-2414 refund, Client Services, “No rush…confirm.”
- Rejected: REQ-2410 invoice, Field Sales, second attempt; REQ-2411 refund, Field Sales, no rush; REQ-2415 invoice, Regional Ops, regional-office wording; REQ-2416 invoice, Finance Desk, scanned; REQ-2417 shipment, Field Sales, second attempt; REQ-2418 refund, Field Sales, scanned.

Tentative: A may work for Regional Ops/Client Services refunds and Regional Ops invoice with no-rush/confirm wording. Avoid A for Field Sales; do not use A for invoice + “regional office” or scanned/Finance Desk.

Option B: accepted REQ-2419 shipment, Regional Ops, “before end of day.” Supports B for explicit urgency, at least shipment. No non-urgent B evidence.

Sender desk alone does not determine validity; request type + exact clue wording matters. “Second attempt,” “scanned,” and truncation did not make A valid.

Option D untested.

Next: avoid A for Field Sales; try B for urgency; use A only for plausible accepted combos above; use C only if exact success combo recurs. Track D.
